analysis.title: Markets On The Move - APAC Equity Outflows Extend Amid Fragile Sentiment; USDTWD Bid
key_insights: Japan: estimated passive turnover for the TOPIX annual rebalance at Thursday's close was revised down to $59.0bn from $63.3bn, but is still set to be a record. The UBS pad is 52% better to sell, with outflows from chemicals and trading companies. The desk is buying memory and insurers.
Hong Kong/China: flows are 52% to sell, including 3% in shorts. The desk is selling technology and financials and buying industrials and healthcare.

Taiwan: flows are 58% sellers. TAIEX broke below 47K and tested 46K after Alphabet results missed expectations and free cash flow worsened, which triggered fears of large AI cash burn. The desk has mixed flows in semiconductor bluechips and is buying ASIC names versus selling testing and thermal names.

Korea: local institutions sold $640mn in cash and $110mn in futures, while foreign investors net bought $246mn in cash. KOSPI is consolidating after rallying 10% over the past two sessions, Nasdaq futures are down 1.5%, and there is no clear direction yet on a Samsung shareholder return.
ASEAN: flows are 57% better to sell, most active in Indonesia. Consumer names see broad support across Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines, while financials and technology flows are mixed.
India: flows are 3:1 net sell. The desk is selling banks, real estate, telecoms and two wheelers, and buying consumer discretionary and energy.
Australia: flows are 55% sell skewed, concentrated in healthcare and financials. The desk is buying consumer staples.

FX: USDTWD opened around 32.430/450 and saw buying interest from foreign banks again as risk sentiment stayed fragile with equities down 2%. Spot rose from 32.450 to 32.550 into the lunch close even though most USD/Asia pairs traded lower.
Rates: the FOMC voted 10-2 to hold the target range. Hammack and Cook dissented. The hold was expected, but Cook's dissent and the lack of dissents from Logan and Kashkari were not.

Rates: Chair Warsh's press conference set a new meeting schedule starting fall 2027. The FOMC keeps eight meetings, but one will cover monetary policy discussion only, with no rate decision or statement. The committee envisions a six-two split in 2028.

Rates: the market read the schedule change as one less opportunity to hike. The swap curve twist-steepened during and after the press conference, with 5s30s steepening 6bp from the lows. 10y spreads reached -37.8 before fading and closed close to pre-FOMC levels.
earnings_insights: Alphabet results missed expectations and free cash flow worsened, per the UBS Taiwan desk. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hold was expected, but Cook's dissent and the absence of dissents from Logan and Kashkari were surprises.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The market read it as one less opportunity to hike, and the swap curve twist-steepened.

Fears of large AI cash burn after Alphabet's miss and weaker free cash flow, weighing on Taiwan technology.
Record TOPIX passive turnover at Thursday's close.
